subject: BIOC
title: Molecular Mechanisms of Cell Function
description: An introductory course describing the biochemistry and molecular biology of selected key functions of animal cells, including: gene expression; mitochondrial production of metabolic energy; cellular communication with the extra-cellular environment; and regulation of cell division.

restrictions.text: A non-terminal course intended to be followed by BIOC 311; BIOC 312 in the U2 year. Not open to students who have taken or are taking BIOL 201 or ANAT 212.

subject: BIOC
title: Laboratory Methods in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology 1
description: Introduction to key methodologies for the isolation, detection and characterization of proteins, lipids, nucleic acids and subcellular fractions, including spectrophotometry, assays of enzymatic activities and chromatographic and electrophoretic methods. Analysis of biochemical data.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking BIOL 301. Open to students in Biochemistry programs, others with permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOC
title: Written Communication in Biomedical Sciences
description: The structure of scientific papers, the interpretation of scientific data, and citation management. Emphasizes practice in writing manuscript-style papers.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking WCOM 314 or MIMM 301.

subject: BIOC
title: Metabolic Biochemistry
description: The generation of metabolic energy in higher organisms with an emphasis on its regulation at the molecular, cellular and organ level. Chemical concepts and mechanisms of enzymatic catalysis are also emphasized. Included: selected topics in carbohydrate, lipid and nitrogen metabolism; complex lipids and biological membranes; hormonal signal transduction.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 200, BIOL 201 or BIOC 212, CHEM 222 or CHEM 234

subject: BIOC
title: Biochemistry of Macromolecules
description: Gene expression from the start of transcription to the synthesis of proteins, their modifications and degradation. Topics covered: purine and pyrimidine metabolism; transcription and its regulation; mRNA processing; translation; targeting of proteins to specific cellular sites; protein glycosylation; protein phosphorylation; protein turn-over; programmed cell death (apoptosis).

subject: BIOC
title: Laboratory Methods in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology 2
description: Modern molecular-biological methods for isolation and characterization of nucleic acids and for analysis of RNA and protein expression, including: plasmid expression, isolation, restriction and ligation; electrophoretic methods and Western blotting; PCR and qPCR applications; immunofluorescence microscopy and basic bioinformatics approaches.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking BIOL 301. Open to students in Biochemistry programs; others with permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOC
title: Undergraduate Research Project
description: Independent research project with a final written report.

prerequisites.text: MIMM 212 or BIOC 220 or BlOL 301 or an equivalent laboratory course in molecular and cell-biological methods, at least one term of undergraduate studies, and a CGPA of at least 3.0; or permission of instructor. A project proposal form must be completed by the student and instructor and approved by the course coordinator or his/her delegate before the start of the term. Instructors will list project-specific prerequisites with the project description.

restrictions.text: Departmental permission required. Student cannot be supervised by same instructor for two 396 Science courses. S/U option not permitted. Open to students in programs offered by the Faculty of Science only.

notes: Note that enrolment may be limited. Students are advised to start the application process well before the start of the term and to plan for an alternative course in the case that no suitable project is available. Individual projects may be suggested each term which may have project-specific prerequisites. Students may also approach professors to devise their own projects. Some projects may be accessible to students in other disciplines. See https://www.mcgill.ca/science/research/undergraduate-research/science-research-courses for more information about available projects and application forms and procedures

subject: BIOC
title: Biophysical Methods in Biochemistry
description: Applications and fundamental bases of important biophysical techniques used in modern biochemistry research laboratories to isolate, characterize and determine the structure and dynamics of proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules and complexes that underlie life and disease.

subject: BIOC
title: Protein Structure and Function
description: Primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure of enzymes. Active site mapping and site-specific mutagenesis of enzymes. Enzyme kinetics and mechanisms of catalysis. Multienzyme complexes.

prerequisites.text: BIOC 311, BIOC 312 and/or sufficient organic chemistry.

restrictions.text: Intended primarily for students at the U3 level

subject: BIOC
title: Nucleic Acids
description: RNA processing, localization and stability. RNAi mechanisms, regulation and applications. Regulation of DNA replication. Genomics: human genome sequence, regulation and organization. DNA repair mechanisms. Special topics on transgenics, genetic diseases and cancer.

prerequisites.text: BIOC 311, BIOC 312 or permission of instructor

subject: BIOC
title: Membranes and Cellular Signaling
description: An integrated treatment of the properties of biological membranes and of intracellular signaling, including the major role that membranes play in transducing and integrating cellular regulatory signals. Biological membrane organization and dynamics: membrane transport; membrane receptors and their associated effectors; mechanisms of regulation of cell growth, morphology, differentiation and death.

prerequisites.text: BIOC 212 or ANAT 212 or BIOL201, ANAT 262, one of PHGY 209 or BIOL 205; one of BIOC 312 or ANAT 365; BIOC 311 recommended

restrictions.text: This course is also listed as ANAT 458. Not open to students who have taken or are taking ANAT 458.

subject: BIOC
title: Research Laboratory in Biochemistry
description: A laboratory research project and related written review article all performed under the supervision of the same professor.

prerequisites.text: BIOC 320 and permission of the course coordinator and the research director.

restrictions.text: Restricted to Honours students in Biochemistry

notes: Students must obtain consent of a prospective research director and the course coordinator in order to register

subject: BIOC
title: Lipids and Lipoproteins in Disease
description: Structure, function and metabolism of lipids and lipoproteins as they relate to lipid storage diseases, obesity, insulin resistance, diabetes, heart disease, Alzheimers disease and other neurological diseases. Transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms governing the synthesis and degradation of important enzymes, lipids, and lipid transport molecules; role of lipid mediators in signaling pathways and protein modification; assembly and dynamics of lipoproteins and biological membranes; genetic disruptions of lipid regulatory proteins such as cell surface receptors leading to human disease.

subject: BIOC
title: Independent Research
description: Individual work on a project to be performed in a research laboratory.

subject: BIOC
title: Biochemistry of Immune Diseases
description: Current selected topics in immunology. The biochemical mechanisms underlying various immuno-pathologies and the clinical significance of therapeutic interventions.

subject: BIOC
title: Molecular Mechanisms of Disease
description: Reflecting on and communicating the molecular underpinnings of human disease, their clinical significance, and relevance to diagnosis and treatment. The underlying molecular causes of disease, going from mutations in DNA, RNA stability and proteins structure and function.

prerequisites.text: BIOC 311, BIOC 312 or permission of the instructor

subject: BIOC
title: RNA in Disease and Therapeutics
description: Recent advances in understanding the complex role of versatile RNA molecules and related biochemical processes that play a central role in homeostasis. The broad spectrum of pathological states resulting from dysregulated RNA and RNA-based therapeutics are presented.

prerequisites.text: BIOC 312 (or equivalent), BIOC 320 or BIOL 301, or permission of the instructor

subject: BIOC
title: Lipids and Lipoproteins in Disease
description: Structure, function, biogenesis, metabolism and roles of lipids and lipoproteins as they relate to lipid storage diseases, obesity, insul inresistance, diabetes, heart disease, Alzheimer's disease and other neurological diseases. Genetic disruptions of lipid regulatory proteins such as cell surface receptors and their consequences on human health.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken BIOC 470.

subject: BIOC
title: Advanced Strategies in Genetics and Genomics
description: Advanced technologies and methods in genomics research, presented by experts actively pursuing the experimental approaches discussed.

restrictions.text: Must take part in the Biochemistry graduate program

subject: BIOC
title: Genomics and Gene Expression
description: Examination of recent developments in analysis of eukaryotic cell genomes and control of gene expression during differentiation and growth control. Molecular genetics; genomics and the bioinformatics of analysis of genomic and functional-genomic data; mechanisms and signal-transduction pathways for regulation of gene expression; applications to human disease with a strong emphasis on cancer.

subject: BIOC
title: Macromolecular Structure
description: X-Ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, Electron Microscopy. Theory and methods used to determine macromolecular structures will be covered. Several practical sessions with hands-on experience for students are included.
notes: Offered in the Winter term, in even alternate years.

subject: BIOC
title: Protein Biology and Proteomics
description: Examination of recent developments in protein biology and proteomics analysis. Proteomics, modeling and biophysical approaches to characterize the functional interactions of biological macromolecules; applications to biological problems. Lectures and in-class discussions are supplemented by practical training in proteomics.

prerequisites.text: BIOC 450 or equivalent, or permission of instructor.

subject: BIOC
title: Seminars in Chemical Biology 1
description: First multidisciplinary seminar in chemical biology.

restrictions.text: Open only to students registered for the M.Sc. or Ph.D. Graduate Option in Chemical Biology.

subject: BIOC
title: Seminars in Chemical Biology 2
description: Third multidisciplinary seminar in chemical biology.

restrictions.text: Open only to students registered for the M.Sc. or Ph.D. Graduate Option in Chemical Biology.

subject: BIOC
title: Biochemistry of Lipoproteins
description: Structure, function and metabolism of lipids and lipoproteins as they relate to lipid storage diseases, obesity, diabetes and heart disease.

restrictions.text: Open to graduate students only with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOC
title: Thesis Research 1 - Bioinformatics
description: Laboratory research focusing on the thesis research project for the M.Sc. degree in Biochemistry; Bioinformatics Option.

restrictions.text: Open to students enrolled in the M.Sc. in Biochemistry (Bioinformatics Option) program.

subject: BIOC
title: Thesis Research 1 (Chemical - Biology)
description: Research toward completion of thesis.

restrictions.text: Open only to students registered for the M.Sc. Graduate Option in Chemical Biology.

subject: BIOC
title: Seminars in Biochemistry
description: Seminars in biochemistry.

restrictions.text: Open to M.Sc. and Ph.D. Biochemistry students only.

title: Thesis Research 1
description: Independent research work under the direction of the Thesis Supervisor and the Supervisory Committee.
